title: Observability
goal: Structured cycle-status logging, a minimal alert webhook so a stuck or degraded cycle actually pages someone, and protocol-fee-brick detection on the canonical pool.
steps: Add structured JSON logging per stage transition (console.error/console.log with a fixed schema, no dependency)
Add a cycle-status projection consumed by the dashboard
Add a minimal alert webhook fired on DEGRADED/FAILED/lease-contention transitions
Add one integration test that actually fires the webhook against a mock endpoint (closing the 'no alert channel has ever been test-fired' gap noted in ops/HANDOFF.md)

Add protocol-fee-monitor.mjs: poll StateLibrary.getSlot0's protocol-fee field for the canonical pool on every scheduler tick (piggybacking on the existing budget-gate pool-state read, no extra RPC call) and fire the same alert-webhook path the instant it goes nonzero — before the next swap even hits the hook's revert, per design.md section 3.7's governance-brick risk
Add a test simulating a nonzero protocol fee appearing on a fixture pool-state read and asserting the alert fires exactly once, not once per subsequent tick
acceptance: Status projection reflects live journal state
A DEGRADED/FAILED transition fires a webhook, proven by an integration test, not just code inspection
A simulated nonzero protocol-fee reading fires the alert webhook on the first tick it appears, deduplicated on subsequent ticks
notes: Intentionally not a full alerting stack; the simplest thing that actually pages someone. Protocol-fee monitoring answers owner decision D11's monitoring-only baseline (option a) regardless of which further option the owner later picks; it does not block on D11's answer.
